newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds bounce back slightly after losses.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds bounce back slightly after losses.

text.p: Argentine bonds bounced back slightly Wednesday after a sharp sell-off on Tuesday.
The market was buoyed by expectations that Congress will achieve quorum for the government's tax-hiking measures which it is due to debate later in the day.
After Tuesday's sell-off, "the market could still see some short-covering," said a trader at a large Argentine bank.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.10 to 117.90, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 1/4 to 82-6/8.
On Tuesday, the Bocon Pre 2 plummeted $0.80 and the FRB shed 1-1/8.

Market players said they would be watching the U.S. Treasuries market closely again after the declines Tuesday on renewed fears of a rate hike by the Federal Reserve this month. The trader suggested that as long as U.S. rates remain stable Argentine bonds are likely to regain their vigor.
On the negative side, Argentina's fiscal deficit may reach $4.5 billion in 1997, the government said in a letter of intent to the International Monetary Fund released Tuesday.
That was much higher than the $3.0 billion deficit next year anticipated in the 1997 budget blueprint that Economy Minister Roque Fernandez sent to Congress last week.
